sources.support: Canonical-source boundary: the cited URL is The Register's verified original article; the company statements remain reported executive observations, not first-party company pages or adjudicated findings. Snowflake CISO Brad Jones told the publication that Snowflake had seen applicants fitting the DPRK-linked category and had shared associated indicators with peers. Netskope CISO James Robinson said Netskope had received fraudulent-worker applications; he described resumes apparently built from stolen or fake identities, an FBI briefing involving security, HR and legal, recruiter detection of copied profiles, and applicants withdrawing when stronger onboarding checks were required. Normalized boundary: Snowflake's CISO said the company had seen applicants fitting the DPRK-linked fraudulent-worker category and shared related indicators with partners and peers. The article does not establish a successful hire or definitive legal identity for any applicant.
